F0009.reason: Answered in the bulk by Y. Han, arXiv:2504.15992 (2025): all singular values in [kappa n^{1/2}, (2-kappa) n^{1/2}] are distinct with probability 1-e^{-cn}; the part near zero and near the edge needs new ideas.
why: Lyons' question whether an m-dependent determinantal process on Z with a degree-m trigonometric-polynomial symbol is an (m+1)-block factor of an i.i.d. sequence; it joins determinantal structure to the coding theory of finitely dependent processes.
Known for m = 1. An unaudited attempt on file treats the sublattice case.

P0347.reason: Too vaguely posed for a target, and the beta-splitting asymptotics around it moved in 2026 (arXiv:2608.18320).
why: Open question 3 of Aidekon, Hu and Shi on discounted tree sums: the Hausdorff dimension of the rays whose local times grow at a prescribed quadratic rate.
The quadratic growth is Theorem 1.6(ii) of the source (2024); the spectrum asks for the standard multifractal analysis on the boundary of the tree.

F0020.reason: Q. Berger and H. Lacoin, arXiv:2509.08789 (2025), give upper bounds on the critical point shift of the random walk pinning model for the simple random walk on Z^d, d >= 3, the first known (their abstract: 'for which no upper bound on the critical point shift was previously known'); with the lower bounds of Birkner-Sun, Berger-Toninelli and the companion arXiv:2509.08769 the question is close to answered for that walk. Whether the bounds match in every dimension was not checked.
why: Lyons' conjecture that an equivariant determinantal process on a group lies, in the stochastic order, between the product measures of densities FK(Q) and 1 - FK(I - Q), FK the Fuglede-Kadison determinant, and that these bounds are optimal; it would extend the Lyons-Steif domination theorem from Z^d to every group.
Proved for stationary determinantal processes on Z^d, with the bounds optimal (Lyons and Steif, 2003; Theorem 5.2 of the source). The source says the conjecture is open even for finite groups.
